first_run.title: Deploy sgit in your own environment, from a CI pipeline: one Docker image, ciphertext in your own S3 bucket in the region you choose, an access token only you hold, and the pipeline pattern we learned building the AgentiCCells site factory, a protected environment, AWS through OpenID Connect with no keys, a role that trusts one repository and one environment, check workflows before anything real, and a full cycle that deploys, tests and tears down

Policies in practice: four places a behaviour policy earns its keep, measured on a real Google key whose reach is five APIs while the feature uses one, a signed policy for the factory's CI changes, requests that carry the policies they act under, and release notes that say what each fix closes and what it must not open

first_run.title: An inbox only your agents can write to: a conductor publishes one append lane per agent, each lane's token sealed to that agent's own key, so everything needed to talk privately is public and only the right agent can use it
sgit in GitHub Actions, side by side: a showcase repository and site that runs four ways of moving a vault between jobs on every run, measured, with a budget for its LLM steps
Attacks rewritten as mandates: 28 supply-chain incidents, the column each one was missing, and why the next maintainer is an agent
Cedar and the policy vault: a debrief on the policy language agents are adopting, where our behaviour policies and sgit vaults meet it, and a brief for the MVP
Where a check runs is part of the policy: tests as enforcers of Agent Behaviour Policies, and what moving them out of the agent's environment would gain, measured on this newsroom

The sidecar repository: a second repository the agent cannot write to, which checks every release against the policy, trusts signed checks instead of re-running them, and is the only thing that deploys, designed for an agent that is fully compromised

The site factory works: three AgentiCCells sites made by hand, then one made by a commit in two minutes and thirty-nine seconds, live over https with a first version written by Claude Code, and the long list of what it took to make something that hard look easy

Our companies and UTH: each company, technology and website we have built, mapped to what UAlgTec Heritage needs to build a European HeritageTech sector, from SGit's vaults and pki.sgit.ai's keys to SHarness, Agent Behaviour Policies, RiskMandate, AgentiCCells and its site factory, GAMMA-Ray, VoiceDebrief and PrompTugal.news, with what each could do for a heritage team, and why a sector needs companies like these

Your own agentic cell, end to end: how a person asks for a site like the ones we made for Yiheng Wang and Silvio Switha, through a key pair in the browser, a vault they fill themselves and the site factory, with only three human gates, and then continues in their own Claude on their own repository
PKI everywhere: from now on every message, secret and handover starts with a signature, and how an agent gets its first key
A pen and a key: a place on every page to mark it, comment on it and tell the newsroom, and a browser key that pki.sgit.ai vouches for, so a note can be checked as mine
Chainguard, mapped: what it builds, what it publishes, how far up the stack its context goes, and where an open behaviour policy and an encrypted vault could plug in
Behaviour policies from the checks: 57 checks taken apart into the 8 behaviours they protect, and where each one is actually kept
Agentics, ready to sell: what we showed at Agentic Engineering Live, who else is selling agentic services and at what price, the engagement path, and a marketplace for the consultants who deliver it

The email agentic cell: why connecting Gmail to agents the usual way is a security mess, and the architecture we will build instead, with one gateway agent that alone touches Gmail, a digital twin of the mailbox in a vault that people and agents work on together, signed proposals, approvals and even reads on append lanes, and behaviour policies at five altitudes

The intersection: SGit, SHarness, Agent Behaviour Policies, RiskMandate and AgentiCCells as one stack of separate companies, now with real customers, real usage and real examples, one ladder of offers on every site, and a plan to align them all

One commit, one site, one owner: the small change to the AgentiCCells site factory that unblocked the most, giving a GitHub account access to the repository it creates, so that one commit with a site's details and its owner's account makes the repository, the DNS record in AWS, the address, HTTPS and the owner's access in under a minute, and all that is left is to point Claude at it
Are hooks the sweet spot? Moving an agent's rules from hope into hooks, rule by rule, until enforcement moves off the machine
